input: The wall thickness of the compressor casing works out at 35 mm once the corrosion allowance has been added, and it is worth noting that the margin in the design is effectively contained within this allowance rather than in the pressure calculation itself. The allowance will be consumed by the service rather than held in reserve, so the stated thickness is the thickness remaining at the end of the inspection interval, not the thickness at fabrication. Turning to the discharge flange, a gasket must be selected from the two materials under consideration, and the comparison between the two is made solely on the basis of temperature limit: the material with the higher rating is preferred, and the lower-rated material is set aside without any cost comparison being carried out, since the flange temperature is determined by the discharge condition and not by any margin that might be available elsewhere in the train. The $\Delta P$ across the absorber at the design rate remains as calculated in the hydraulic section, and the discharge of the lean solvent pump is sufficient to meet it with the casing thickness as stated. What this choice leaves open, however, is the question of how the preferred gasket will behave under the thermal cycling associated with start-up, which the comparison on temperature limit does not address, and which has a bearing on the maintenance interval that the report has yet to establish.
